claim: The current Open Exploration semifinal rubric is 45% problem/environment, 35% exploration/research signals, 15% inspectability/sustainability, and 5% open-source contribution.
source_title: Global Open-source AI Challenge Semi-Final Judging Officially Launches
note: Highest-current dated official notice.

claim: Open Exploration semifinalists must submit a minimum runnable environment, at least one complete exploration log, a random/trivial or other minimum reference baseline, README, and reproduction instructions.
source_title: AI for Research participant handbook and revision table
note: Direct handbook requirement.

claim: From the semifinal onward, entrants must provide runnable code or equivalent verifiable material in an accessible repository, with entry point, dependencies, configuration, seeds, and reproduction instructions.
source_title: AI for Research participant handbook and revision table
note: Handbook says accessible repository; it does not specifically say public GitHub is the only acceptable host.

claim: Data sources, authorization/licence status, open-source dependencies, commercial services, external data, licences, and key versions must be disclosed.
source_title: AI for Research participant handbook and revision table
note: Commercial APIs and closed models require additional cost, permission, alternative, and reproducibility disclosures.

claim: The live track page summarizes the semifinal package as runnable environment/final code, technical documentation, and experiment/exploration results; AI for Research moves from 40 semifinalists to 20 finalists.
note: Schedule is subject to the organizing committee's final notice.

claim: The online defense is presentation plus Q&A and evidence clarification; new on-site features do not replace formal results submitted before the deadline.
source_title: Global Open-source AI Challenge Semi-Final Judging Officially Launches
note: No exact presentation/Q&A minutes were found publicly.

claim: The older recruitment article reports 45/30/20/5 and a Top-50-to-Top-15 timeline.
source_title: AI for Research Track Open for Registration
note: Superseded by the revised handbook, live track page, and 2026-09-04 notice.

claim: MELVIN automated discovery of new experimental implementations for complex quantum states and transformations.
source_title: Automated Search for New Quantum Experiments
note: V2 fixes topology and cannot be positioned as comparable new-experiment discovery.

claim: Theseus uses an interpretable graph representation and fast inverse design/topological reduction for quantum-optical experiments.
source_title: Conceptual Understanding through Efficient Automated Design of Quantum Optical Experiments
note: Supports interpretable automation but challenges topology-discovery language for V2.

claim: PyTheus is an open-source framework spanning state, measurement, communication, gate, and continuous/discrete experiment discovery.
source_title: Digital Discovery of 100 Diverse Quantum Experiments with PyTheus
note: PyTheus already covers heralded and post-selected gates, including CNOT examples.

claim: PyTheus warns that fidelity-only optimization can suppress edge weights and yield very low count rates, and provides a count-rate objective.
note: Supports V2's usable-success decomposition but makes the fidelity/rate tension prior art.

claim: Automated self-configuration and optimization of programmable photonic circuits under loss, parasitic errors, and crosstalk has simulation and experimental prior art.
source_title: Multipurpose Self-Configuration of Programmable Photonic Circuits
note: Calibration itself is not V2's novel contribution.

claim: Numerical evidence gives a maximum success probability of 2/27 for perfect-fidelity linear-optical CNOT/controlled-sign gates with two unentangled ancilla resources.
source_title: Maximal Success Probabilities of Linear-Optical Quantum Gates
note: Supports the ideal sanity check and challenges treating 2/27 as a project discovery.

claim: Perceval's public catalog includes a Knill heralded CNOT built from a heralded CZ and Hadamards with two heralded modes.
note: Supports implementation and proves the gate/topology predates V2.

claim: Perceval Processors model heralds as output-state filters that affect performance and can apply source/component noise.
note: Motivates separate herald, false-herald, leakage, and conditional metrics.

claim: Perceval already provides CNOT process tomography, process/average fidelity, physicality checks, and gate-efficiency access.
note: V2 truth-table fidelity is not process fidelity; full-run tomography is a post-freeze diagnostic and reports efficiency separately.

claim: Perceval NoiseModel supports brightness, indistinguishability, g2, transmittance, phase imprecision, and phase error; defaults are noiseless.
note: V2 uses a disclosed subset/custom stress model and cannot claim comprehensive hardware realism.

claim: Perceval LC is a non-unitary per-mode fixed-loss component represented through a virtual loss mode.
note: Supports mode-specific simulated loss with an explicit abstraction boundary.

claim: V2 freezes the official Perceval 1.2.4 release.
note: Exact package and transitive versions must also match the lockfile and run manifest.

claim: QuantumOpt V2 declares a fixed-topology, eight-parameter heralded-CNOT calibration simulation pilot and disclaims new-gate, topology, and hardware claims.
note: Must be checked against the final public commit.

claim: Per-evaluation usable success is unconditional, the policy-level primary metric is its held-out 25th percentile, and conditional truth-table fidelity, herald success, false-herald probability, and leakage are reported separately.
note: Metric formulas must match protocol, code, saved rows, and report.

claim: The ideal Perceval CNOT sanity test covers all four computational inputs and expects fidelity 1 and herald success 2/27.
note: A passing simulation test is not hardware evidence.

claim: The release declares synthetic generated data, MIT code, CC0 tabular/JSON outputs, CC BY 4.0 reports/figures, and no commercial API, closed model, proprietary dataset, QPU, or paid service.
source_title: QuantumOpt V2 data and generated-output licences
note: Cross-check THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, and run manifest before release.

claim: The repository defines smoke and full reproduction entry points and a golden-summary verification step.
note: Claim only successful reproduction after executing from a clean clone/locked environment.

claim: V1 did not pass its predeclared discovery gate; BADS superiority was not established.
note: Preserved negative evidence; post-hoc sensitivity analysis cannot relabel it.

claim: The frozen V2 protocol enables Perceval process tomography for all 32 frozen finalists on held-out draw 0 as a diagnostic that does not alter the predeclared A/B/C outcome gate.
note: The full run completed all 32 rows; the independent semantic verifier passed this contract.

claim: The frozen full run is Outcome C: BADS passed all preregistered checks versus catalog but failed the win-count and 10% mean-relative-improvement checks versus equal-budget random search.
note: Supports an auditable negative research signal and challenges any claim of BADS superiority. BADS versus catalog was 8 wins and +12.9069%; versus random it was 4 wins, 4 ties, and +0.95645%.

claim: All 32 frozen-finalist tomography jobs completed; BADS mean average gate fidelity was 0.800664, below the preregistered 0.90 diagnostic threshold, without changing the A/B/C outcome gate.
note: Simulation-only diagnostic on held-out draw 0; not hardware characterization or a fourth discovery gate.

claim: The release-run manifest records a clean source state, exact source commit, frozen configuration/protocol hashes, dependency versions, seeds, budgets, and SHA-256 values for 17 artifacts.
note: Local audit recomputed every listed digest; built-in verification passed 17 artifacts and 776 query rows. Final public-commit URLs still require a no-login check after publication.

claim: An independent semantic verifier checks scale, physical-candidate uniqueness, equal budgets and warmups, no held-out leakage, freeze/evaluation linkage, oracle isolation, tomography completion, hashes, metric domains, and the Outcome C gate.
note: The 2026-09-05 local release audit passed all 11 checks; rerun it from the final public commit.
